# Landing page
**Route:** `/liivv-health/diabetes-care`  
**Source:** `core/messages/en.json` → `DiabetesCare.ui.landingPage`; structure in `diabetes-care/landing-meta.ts`  
**Generated:** 2026-10-08 from commit `f7f9ef0b` — do not edit this file by hand; see [README](../README.md).

> Every word of the landing, in the order the page renders it. References drop the leading `ui.landingPage.`. There are no testimonials and no unsourced numbers on the page: the four invented "voices" and the "10k+ / 24/7 / 19+ / 1 calm place" band are gone, and every number now names its source. On /fr the landing’s French ships flagged as machine translated (French review gate `landing` decides the draft marker on previews).

## The fact band (#facts)

*Four numbers, each with the sources it rests on printed under it on the page. They replace the unsourced "10k+", "24/7", "19+" and "1 calm place" band.*

- `facts.label` — Diabetes facts and their sources
- `facts.eyebrow` — A few facts
- `facts.heading` — Diabetes comes in more than one kind.
- `facts.sourcesLabel` — Sources
- **5 to 10%** `facts.items.1.value` of people with diabetes have type 1. It can start in adulthood too. `facts.items.1.label`  
  *Sources: Type 1 Diabetes (Diabetes Canada)*
- **90 to 95%** `facts.items.2.value` of diabetes cases in Canada are type 2, the most common type. Some people with it have no symptoms at all. `facts.items.2.label`  
  *Sources: Type 2 Diabetes (Diabetes Canada)*
- **3 to 20%** `facts.items.3.value` of pregnant people develop gestational diabetes, depending on their risk factors. It usually goes away after birth. `facts.items.3.label`  
  *Sources: Gestational Diabetes (Diabetes Canada)*
- **About 71%** `facts.items.4.value` of people with type 1 in Canada were diagnosed as adults, by one estimate. `facts.items.4.label`  
  *Sources: Facts and figures (Breakthrough T1D Canada (formerly JDRF))*

## Questions (#faq)

*The first question is open; the rest are closed. Each answer lists its sources under it on the page. A question whose answer waits on a switch is left out whole — the page never shows a question without its answer.*

- `faq.label` — Frequently asked questions
- `faq.heading` — Questions, answered with sources.
- `faq.note` — Practical notes, not medical advice. Each answer lists where it comes from.

**Can I order my supplies here, and will my plan pay?** `faq.items.1.q`

You can order diabetes supplies such as meters, strips, lancets, pen needles, sensors and pump supplies from the shelf. Liivv’s pharmacies serve all of Canada, Quebec and the territories included, but insulin can’t be ordered online for delivery in Quebec. To fill a prescription, send it from your account’s Pharmacy page: choose Add prescription, then transfer it from your current pharmacy or ask your doctor to fax it. What’s covered for pumps, sensors, strips and needles is different in each province and territory, and Diabetes Canada compares them by province and territory. Coverage changes, so check the date on each comparison and confirm with your provincial or territorial plan. Our pharmacy in your province bills your provincial drug plan directly for what it covers, except in Quebec, where orders are paid for privately. Other programs each pay their own way: where one pays you back, we can give you an invoice for your claim. Check how yours pays before you order, or ask Liivv’s Certified Diabetes Educators. `faq.items.1.a`

*Sources: Comparisons by Province/Territory (Diabetes Canada); National pharmacare bilateral agreements (Health Canada); National pharmacare (BC PharmaCare) (Government of British Columbia (PharmaCare)); Stays Outside Québec (Gouvernement du Québec); Ontario Monitoring for Health Program (Diabetes Canada, running an Ontario government program); The New Brunswick Insulin Pump Program (IPP) (Government of New Brunswick)*  
*About Liivv, rests on the owner’s word (2026-10-05, and the answers of 2026-10-06).*  
*Link: "your account’s Pharmacy page" → a Liivv page, `/account/pharmacy` (/fr gets the /fr prefix)*  
*Link: "compares them by province and territory" → the source `dc-comparisons-by-province` (Comparisons by Province/Territory (Diabetes Canada))*  

**How private is my order?** `faq.items.2.q` *(held until `adSignalsShipped` is switched on — not rendered, and not sent to the browser while held)*

On Diabetes Care pages, on diabetes product pages, and in a cart with diabetes supplies, we turn off advertising signals. What you read and buy there isn’t used for ads or to build ad audiences. The page address and title are left out of our site analytics, and so are the names of diabetes products. `faq.items.2.a`

*About Liivv, rests on how the code on this branch behaves.*  

**What if a sensor stops working or comes off early?** `faq.items.3.q`

A sensor can be up to 15 minutes slower than a finger-prick check to show your blood sugar, so keep a meter and strips as a backup, where you can reach them. Liivv’s Certified Diabetes Educators can help with sensor and supply questions: call 1-844-561-1254, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern, except holidays. If someone can’t swallow, is unconscious or is having a seizure, call 911. For a low, a high or a sick day, go to Staying Safe. `faq.items.3.a`

*Sources: Technology & Devices (Diabetes Canada); What is glucagon? (Breakthrough T1D Canada (formerly JDRF)); Glucagon: What it is and how to use it (Diabetes@School (Canadian Paediatric Society, CPEG and Diabetes Canada)); Chapter 14: 2023 Update – Hypoglycemia in Adults (Diabetes Canada, Clinical Practice Guidelines)*  
*About Liivv, rests on the owner’s word (2026-10-05, and the answers of 2026-10-06).*  
*Link: "call 1-844-561-1254" → `tel:+18445611254`*  
*Link: "call 911" → `tel:911`*  
*Link: "Staying Safe" → Staying Safe · `staying-safe`*  

**Where do used needles, lancets and sensor applicators go?** `faq.items.4.q`

Into a sharps container. In Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island, the Health Products Stewardship Association (HPSA) gives out free sharps containers at participating collection locations, such as pharmacies. When yours is full, seal it and return it to a drop-off location. Its program takes lancets, pen tips (pen needles), syringes, infusion sets and sensor (CGM) applicators with needles. It doesn’t take glucose meters. Never put used sharps in the garbage or the recycling. Elsewhere in Canada, ask your pharmacy: many pharmacies supply safe, puncture-proof containers. `faq.items.4.a`

*Sources: Returning Medical Sharps (Health Products Stewardship Association); Getting Started with Insulin (Diabetes Canada)*  

**Can I order insulin here?** `faq.items.5.q` *(`insulinReviewConfirmed` is on — live — not rendered, and not sent to the browser while held)*

Yes. Insulin is listed in the shop. A pharmacist reviews and dispenses every insulin and glucagon order, shipped in plain packaging. Insulin is shipped cold-chain. Insulin can’t be ordered online for delivery in Quebec. Your health-care team works with you to decide on your insulin and how you take it, and we don’t give dosing advice. Storage is different for each insulin. Follow its product information, or ask your pharmacist. `faq.items.5.a`

*Sources: Getting Started with Insulin (Diabetes Canada)*  
*About Liivv, rests on the owner’s word (2026-10-05, and the answers of 2026-10-06).*  
*Shown on /en only: insulin may not be advertised to Quebec (B11), so the question is not rendered on /fr and not sent to the French browser.*

Please read the publisher column: it is where a manufacturer grant, a single province or a single hospital shows. "Locator" is the reviewer-only paraphrase kept in `sources-review.ts` — it is never rendered on a page, and it is what a claim in this file should be checked against.*

| `dc-cpg-ch14-hypoglycemia-2023` | Chapter 14: 2023 Update – Hypoglycemia in Adults | Diabetes Canada, Clinical Practice Guidelines | Canadian guideline or position statement | Paraphrase: level 1 often 3.0–3.9, level 2 often below 3.0, level 3 any reading that needs help from someone else; treat with 15 g of fast carbohydrate, recheck in 15 minutes and retreat if still below 3.9; prescribe glucagon to people at high risk, such as insulin users, with teaching for their support persons; a severe low is treated with intranasal or injectable glucagon (doses on the page, not used on the site). Always link this update: the old /chapter-14 still loads with older guidance (retreat below 4.0; 1 mg glucagon only). Table 4: 150 mL juice or regular soft drink; 6 Life Savers; 15 mL honey. The effectiveness of glucagon is reduced after more than 2 standard alcoholic drinks in the previous few hours (used on Staying Safe card 4, ruling C2). Ruled 2026-10-06 (C1): 3.9 site-wide; 4.0 only for driving (Ch21). Ruled 2026-10-06 (C13): the site uses Table 4’s 150 mL (⅔ cup). Ruled 2026-10-06 (C29): Table 4’s 6 Life Savers differs from the 4 on the 02/24 sheet, and the brand is left out. | <https://www.diabetes.ca/for-professionals/full-guidelines/chapter-14-2023-update> |
